claim: Aging is characterized by extensive metabolic reprogramming.
source: Aging is characterized by extensive metabolic reprogramming.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that is supported by the subsequent experimental findings in the manuscript.

claim: Levels of tyrosine were increased with age in long-lived flies.
source: Among the metabolites that changed, levels of tyrosine were increased with age in long-lived flies.
evidence: This claim is supported by metabolomic data presented in Figure 1B showing tyrosine levels in 1-week and 4-week-old flies.

claim: The levels of enzymes in the tyrosine degradation pathway increase with age in wild-type flies.
source: We demonstrate that the levels of enzymes in the tyrosine degradation pathway increase with age in wild-type flies.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1D showing increased mRNA levels of tyrosine degradation pathway enzymes in 5-week-old vs 1-week-old flies.

claim: Whole-body downregulation of enzymes in the tyrosine degradation pathway significantly extends Drosophila lifespan.
source: Whole-body and neuronal-specific downregulation of enzymes in the tyrosine degradation pathway significantly extends Drosophila lifespan
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data shown in Figure 3A-D demonstrating lifespan extension with RNAi knockdown of tyrosine degradation pathway enzymes.

claim: Neuronal-specific downregulation of enzymes in the tyrosine degradation pathway significantly extends Drosophila lifespan.
source: Whole-body and neuronal-specific downregulation of enzymes in the tyrosine degradation pathway significantly extends Drosophila lifespan
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data shown in Figure 3G-I demonstrating lifespan extension with neuronal-specific RNAi knockdown.

claim: Downregulation of tyrosine degradation pathway enzymes causes alterations of metabolites associated with increased lifespan.
source: Whole-body and neuronal-specific downregulation of enzymes in the tyrosine degradation pathway significantly extends Drosophila lifespan, causes alterations of metabolites associated with increased lifespan
evidence: This is supported by metabolomic profiling data shown in Figure 4 identifying metabolites that change with TAT downregulation.

claim: Downregulation of tyrosine degradation pathway enzymes upregulates the levels of tyrosine-derived neuromediators.
source: Whole-body and neuronal-specific downregulation of enzymes in the tyrosine degradation pathway significantly extends Drosophila lifespan, causes alterations of metabolites associated with increased lifespan, and upregulates the levels of tyrosine-derived neuromediators.
evidence: This is supported by neurotransmitter quantification data shown in Figure 5 demonstrating increased levels of dopamine, octopamine, and tyramine in TAT mutant flies.

claim: Feeding wild-type flies with tyrosine increased their lifespan.
source: Moreover, feeding wild-type flies with tyrosine increased their lifespan.
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B demonstrating lifespan extension with low-dose tyrosine supplementation.

claim: Suppression of ETC complex I drives the upregulation of enzymes in the tyrosine degradation pathway.
source: Mechanistically, we show that suppression of ETC complex I drives the upregulation of enzymes in the tyrosine degradation pathway
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6A demonstrating increased TAT mRNA levels with RNAi knockdown of ETC complex I subunits.

claim: Tigecycline can rescue the upregulation of tyrosine degradation pathway enzymes caused by ETC complex I suppression.
source: Mechanistically, we show that suppression of ETC complex I drives the upregulation of enzymes in the tyrosine degradation pathway, an effect that can be rescued by tigecycline, an FDA-approved drug that specifically suppresses mitochondrial translation.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6F,G demonstrating that Tigecycline treatment suppresses TAT upregulation induced by ETC complex I inhibition.

claim: Tyrosine supplementation partially rescued lifespan of flies with ETC complex I suppression.
source: In addition, tyrosine supplementation partially rescued lifespan of flies with ETC complex I suppression.
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D demonstrating partial lifespan rescue with tyrosine supplementation in flies with NP15.6 RNAi.

claim: The rate of death from tyrosine toxicity correlated with the strength of the RNAi lines.

claim: The lifespan was either non-affected in male wild-type flies or decreased at the highest (5X and 10X) concentrations by a much lower extent in female wild-type flies.
